summary: Sudden 5xx elevation during large sparse-embedding upload causing accept-queue collapse
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexicoAI reported a sudden increase in 5xx responses starting 2026-03-13 18:12 UTC. Spikes correlate with a single large sparse embedding upload job from the customer (multipart/streaming upload of 12M sparse vectors). API gateway returned 502/503/504 intermittently and several upstream runtime workers reported socket exhaustion and short-lived OOMs.

Impact:
- LexicoAI experienced ~60% request failure rate for embedding requests to model embed-sparse-v2 for approximately 35 minutes.
- Multiple downstream applications (search indexing pipelines) retried and amplified traffic.

Environment:
- prod - us-east-1
- Customer on enterprise plan using dedicated tenant pool (tenant-id: t-lexico-09).

Observed behavior / Error patterns:
- apigw logs show increased connection resets and 502/504 status codes.
- Ingress proxy queues for tenant t-lexico-09 reached high accept-queue length and then collapsed (dropped connections).
- Serving runtime logs show repeated short-lived worker OOMs and "too many open files" / EMFILE on ephemeral sockets.

Initial hypothesis: large multipart sparse embedding upload caused a very high rate of concurrent small write operations which saturated ephemeral socket table and accept queue; cascading retries from client and API gateway hedged retries amplified load, triggering runtime accept-queue collapse and transient OOMs.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer ran bulk embedding upload using their SDK with chunk_size=128, parallel_uploads=64, total_vectors=12,000,000.
2) Multiple clients in customer pipeline issued concurrent requests to /v1/embeddings with small per-request payloads in streaming mode.
3) Observe apigw and ingress proxy metrics: accept queue length spikes then drops, followed by 502/504 responses and runtime worker restarts.
4) Re-running with lower parallelism and larger chunk_size reproduces much lower error rate.
logs_snippets:
- apigw: 2026-03-13T18:12:30Z apigw[tenant=t-lexico-09] ERROR upstream returned 502 (connection reset)
- ingress-proxy: 2026-03-13T18:15:02Z proxy[tid=7] WARN accept-queue-length=812 -> drop policy triggered
- runtime: 2026-03-13T18:16:18Z runtime[worker-23] ERROR OOM: allocation failed (eviction failed)
- runtime: 2026-03-13T18:16:19Z runtime[worker-23] ERROR EMFILE: too many open files
investigation_notes:
2026-03-13 18:25 UTC - Support triaged and increased logging; advised customer to pause ingestion.
2026-03-13 18:28 UTC - SRE (Diego Rivera) confirmed accept-queue metric spike correlated with embedders from LexicoAI.
2026-03-13 18:35 UTC - Observed runtime worker EMFILE errors in system journal; kernel fd table per-worker hitting limit.
2026-03-13 18:40 UTC - Found ingress proxy config: per-tenant ephemeral fd soft-limit set to 4096; bulk upload pattern transiently required ~8k fds due to many half-open streaming connections and hedged retries.
2026-03-13 18:45 UTC - KV-cache invalidations observed immediately prior to spike (customer retried failed parts) which caused prefetch and small-model metadata lookups to increase connection churn.
Hypotheses:
- Primary: Accept-queue and ephemeral fd exhaustion caused upstream connection resets leading to 502/504.
- Secondary: Client-side retry logic and aggressive parallel_uploads amplified the initial transient, pushing runtime into OOM and worker restarts.
Evidence collected:
- Kernel fd counters, ingress-proxy fd histograms, apigw retry rate, runtime OOM logs, heap/alloc profiles from affected workers (attached to INT-90412).
mitigation_actions:
- 2026-03-13 18:50 UTC: Rate-limited tenant t-lexico-09 at apigw ingress (throttle to 250 rps) to allow queue to drain.
- 2026-03-13 18:52 UTC: Increased ephemeral fd soft-limit for tenant pool from 4096 -> 8192 as short-term mitigation (rolled via ingress-proxy config bump).
- Advised LexicoAI to pause uploads and reduce parallel_uploads to 8 and increase chunk_size to 2048.
- Applied temporary client-side guide: use exponential backoff with jitter and avoid hedged retries for heavy upload jobs.
resolution:
Work in progress. Short-term measures restored customer traffic to ~95% success by 19:05 UTC after throttling + fd limit bump and customer-side throttling.
Long-term actions (owner assigned):
- SRE to implement per-tenant adaptive ingress backpressure that detects large fanout upload patterns and automatically shapes them (owner: Diego Rivera, INT-90412).
- Platform: add safe defaults to SDK for bulk embedding uploads (lower default parallel_uploads, recommended chunk_size) and improve guidance in developer docs (owner: Developer Experience team, PR linked).
- Runtime: investigate fd leak paths and add stronger acceptance queue metrics/alerts; consider lowering hedged-retry aggressiveness when accept-queue > X.
Follow-ups:
- Scheduled post-incident review and runbook update (confluence page created).
